events.description: HTS offensive took control of Syria; Jolani later dissolved HTS, formed a government and appointed himself president
Hurras al-Din announced it was disbanding and told fighters to prepare for the next stage, after Jolani formed a government
A Hurras al-Din leader killed, suspected US drone strike, 'in the last few weeks'
Iraqi operation in Anbar killed the ISIS deputy governor who facilitated communication between Abu Khadija al-Iraqi and Mumin
Puntland Defense Forces counter-offensive against IS-Somalia; ISIS defending with dozens of kamikaze drones and suicide bombers; recent US operation also had some success
IS-Somalia almost doubled in size from foreign terrorist fighters (Horn/East Africa, Yemen, Tunisia, Libya, Sudan, even Israeli Arabs)
Meetings between Houthi and al-Shabaab leaders: weapons (incl. UAV technology) in exchange for increased piracy in the Gulf of Aden/Red Sea
AQAP–Houthi 'pragmatic agreement': mutual non-aggression, prisoner exchanges, movement of weapons
Khalid Saif al-Adel (Khalid Zaidan), son of Saif al-Adel, killed
actors: Khalid Saif al-Adel (Muhammad Salah al-Din Zaidan)

events.description: Al-Qaeda operative deployed to Kunar to manage al-Qaeda's finances from Iran into Afghanistan
TTP established camps in Kunar, Nangarhar, Khost and Paktika; Jamaat Ansarullah camps in Kunduz and Khost
TTP carried out 600 attacks in the six-month reporting period (more than three a day)
Rumors that JNIM or parts of it are discussing leaving al-Qaeda; report shows deepening AQ integration instead
Six months earlier the UN report had similar language doubting Mumin's appointment as caliph; more member states now accept it

Hurras al-Din's 'disbanding' is likely a public move to relieve pressure on Jolani, mirroring al-Qaeda's low-profile accommodation with the Taliban.
ISIS leadership resides between Abdul Qadir Mumin (Somalia; possibly the caliph, head of al-Karrar) and Abu Khadija al-Iraqi (GDP and Delegated Committee).
IS-Somalia doubled through foreign fighters and fields kamikaze drones and advanced IEDs against the Puntland counter-offensive.

Cross-sectarian cooperation: Houthis arm al-Shabaab for piracy and have a pragmatic non-aggression/prisoner/weapons agreement with AQAP; Fitton-Brown argues Saif al-Adel is pulling AQAP and Shabaab into Iran's axis.
Saif al-Adel in Iran is reorganizing al-Qaeda in Afghanistan and reactivating sleeper cells in Iraq, Syria, Libya and Europe; AQ finances flow from Iran into Afghanistan via Kunar.

The Taliban keep a permissive environment for al-Qaeda (camps in at least 12 provinces, GDI protection for families) and weaponize TTP and the Tajik Taliban against Pakistan and Tajikistan; TTP ran 600 attacks in six months.
Taliban–ISKP rivalry is genuine; claims the Taliban runs ISKP are rejected.
JNIM is deepening ties with other AQ affiliates despite split rumors and is building quasi-state governance while expanding toward the Gulf of Guinea and northwest Nigeria.
